problem.text: Model construction previously selected one config.model_class, while compilation collected only tensors belonging to the selected model's modules. These interfaces lacked explicit component selection and an additional-tensor preservation hook.

reasoning.text: The change separates component construction from checkpoint preservation: callers select one component, but compilation queries every registered component class for additional tensors.

This is consistent with preparation for multimodal checkpoints rather than completed multimodal inference: all supplied registrations remain text components, and Model.from_config explicitly retains a multimodal TODO.

impact.text: Model.from_config defaults to component='text', asserts that the component exists, and instantiates its mapped class. The config attribute changes from model_class to model_classes, so external integrations using the old attribute require adaptation.

source_notes.text: PR #25, “Language layers for Mistral Small 3.1 and InternVL3,” contains turboderp's concern that language-only support could produce checkpoints incompatible with future component models. Its relationship to this task is inferred from the shared component-model design; the discussion does not explicitly identify this commit.

Other matching discussions concern different changes: PR #4, “chore: update config.py,” proposes a spelling correction; issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports extension loading; issue #6, “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr',” reports installation/JIT failure. Their connection here is inferred only from shared config/model paths, not a demonstrated fix.

Issue #33, “Error converting model,” includes a traceback through compile_model's get_tensors call, later identifies too many open files, and subsequently discusses GLM4 output. Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” concerns Cholesky failure during quantization. Shared compilation/conversion paths establish contextual overlap only; attributing either issue's resolution to this refactor would be unsupported.

limitations: No model loading, GPU inference, safetensors serialization, or filesystem round trip was executed.
The scalar check models shard allocation only; it does not execute compile_model.
Pinned model configurations were not inspected, so model-by-model checkpoint compatibility and dimensions remain unestablished.
External callers and dynamically constructed component mappings were not exhaustively validated.

chapters.title: Component selection and preservation of additional tensors

claims.text: Config now stores a component-name-to-class dictionary. Existing architecture constructors supply a text mapping. LlamaConfig accepts an optional derived_model mapping, using the ordinary Llama text mapping when that argument is falsey.

MistralConfig and Qwen2Config explicitly supply their respective model subclasses through derived_model. Previously their inherited LlamaConfig constructor selected LlamaModel. Both selected subclasses delegate construction to LlamaModel, so the inspected change distinguishes class identity without introducing a separate layer implementation.

Model.get_additional_compiled_tensors defaults to an empty dictionary. compile_model merges each registered class's result, expects an n_bytes entry for each tensor, and appends tensor-name strings after the ordinary module entries in its shard plan. Duplicate extra-tensor keys are resolved by dictionary update order.

Writing dispatches on plan-entry type: Module entries load quantized working-directory tensors by prefix and close that collection; string entries load an individual original tensor from config.stc. Both paths request BF16 preservation and contiguous tensors before the existing shard writer and weight-map construction.

Additional tensors use the existing soft shard limit: shard_size is multiplied by 1024² bytes, exact fits stay in the current shard, and an oversized item is not split. Reported n_bytes values contribute to total_size and therefore to multi-shard index metadata.

A bounded Python transcription verified the allocation boundaries with capacity 10: [6,4] stays together, [6,5] separates, and [11] remains one oversized shard. One shard_size unit evaluates to 1,048,576 bytes.

findings.description: The additional-tensor oversize warning references the preceding module variable instead of the current tensor key.
findings.trigger: An additional tensor reports n_bytes greater than max_shard_bytes.
findings.expected_behavior: Identify the oversized additional tensor and continue allocating its shard.
findings.actual_behavior: With ordinary modules present, the warning identifies the last module instead. If model.modules is empty, evaluating module.key raises UnboundLocalError before allocation continues.

verification.description: Inspected the new extra-tensor loop and the preceding module loop. Whole-parent literal caller search found conversion main calling compile_model after its conversion loop. The supplied default hook returns no additional tensors, so this observation concerns nonempty hook implementations rather than demonstrated failures of current text conversions.
verification.limits: No repository execution; literal search does not establish external or dynamic caller coverage.

annotation.summary: Prepares component-based model construction and preserves hook-selected original tensors during compilation, while retaining text as the default component.
